key_catalysts.rationale: The cleanest near-term test of whether the super-long JGB sell-off is a policy repricing or a fiscal risk premium. The 28 August 2-year auction drew a bid-to-cover of 2.97 against a 12-month average of 3.74, and the 25s30s spread is already inverted at -1.0bp. A weak tail would confirm the fiscal channel and be yen-NEGATIVE despite higher yields; a strong auction would let the policy channel dominate.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially. The 30-year is already at 4.09-4.14% and SMBC Nikko has publicly questioned whether demand will materialise, so a weak result is half expected; a genuinely failed auction is not.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY primarily; EUR/JPY and GBP/JPY secondarily since both counterparts have their own long-end fiscal issues

key_catalysts.rationale: July payrolls printed -23,000 against a +95,000 consensus with 103,000 of downward revisions, and average hourly earnings growth has slowed to 3.2%. A second negative print would question the September Fed hike and compress the differential from the US side, which is yen-positive; a strong rebound confirms the hike and is yen-negative.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. The market has resolved the July weakness in favour of the inflation mandate after Warsh's Jackson Hole address, so a second weak print would be a genuine surprise.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY; the cross-yen pairs would move only through the risk channel

key_catalysts.event: Japan revised Q2 GDP and July balance of payments
key_catalysts.rationale: The first preliminary showed +0.3% quarter-on-quarter with capex at -1.2%, but the Ministry of Finance corporate survey published 1 September showed Q2 capital spending up 1.6% year on year against a 0.2% consensus with pre-tax profits up 24.6%, which skews the revision higher. The same release carries the July current account after June's first monthly deficit in seventeen months.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially. The capex beat is public but the GDP revision arithmetic is not widely modelled; the current-account risk is not priced at all.

key_catalysts.event: Japan August corporate goods price index
key_catalysts.rationale: July showed yen-basis import prices up 29.1% year on year against 17.7% in contract-currency terms, an 11.4 percentage point exchange-rate wedge, and a terms-of-trade index of 81.62 down from 90.5 in the first quarter. With Brent at USD 93 and JKM LNG up 101.9% year on year, August should deteriorate further.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. The market does not trade Japanese producer prices, but it is the input to the terms-of-trade series that drives the strategic bearish case.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY; also AUD/JPY and CAD/JPY where the counterpart is a commodity exporter

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision and Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: Roughly 57-66% priced for a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% depending on source - flagged as best available - after three hawkish dissents in July and a June SEP median of 3.8% for end-2026. A hike leaves the 262.5bp differential unchanged and confirms the carry regime; a hold would compress the differential from the US side and is the single largest yen-positive surprise available in the tactical window.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially. A hike is roughly 57-66% priced, so between a third and two fifths of the distribution is a hold, and the new projections are not priced at all.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY above all; it sets the dollar leg for every yen cross

key_catalysts.rationale: July printed 1.9% headline and 1.8% core with the BoJ's own ex-special-factors measure at 2.3%, and government energy subsidies are suppressing the headline by roughly 40-50 basis points. Tokyo core has accelerated three consecutive months and the BoJ expects core 'clearly above 2 percent from the second half of fiscal 2026'.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially. Consensus expects little change; the subsidy-unwind arithmetic and the 2025 rebasing that lowered the year-ago base are not widely modelled.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY; also CHF/JPY where the relative inflation gap is 1.8% against 0.06%

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The largest single event in the tactical window. Approximately 80-90% priced for a 25bp hike to 1.25%, with Takata already dissenting for that level in July. The trade is not the decision but the press conference: whether Ueda repeats the Summary of Opinions formulation that the pace will be 'faster than market expectations'.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the decision, not at all for the pace language. December is priced at only an implied 1.21%, i.e. one hike and no more inside 2026.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Every yen cross; CHF/JPY most cleanly because the counterpart central bank is pinned at zero

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan minutes of the 30-31 July meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: Published ten days AFTER the September decision, which is unusually unhelpful sequencing. The minutes will detail the 8-1 vote and Takata's dissent for 1.25%, and the balance of the discussion will either corroborate or undercut whatever the Board does on 18 September.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. Minutes rarely move the yen but this set carries the record of the meeting that immediately preceded a hike.

key_catalysts.event: US FY2027 appropriations deadline and Japanese interim fiscal half-year end
key_catalysts.rationale: Two coincident events. A US government shutdown is precedented - there were two in 2026 already, in January-February and February-April - and would be risk-negative and therefore yen-positive. Separately, the Japanese interim book-closing on 30 September generates documented repatriation and dividend-related flows.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. The volatility surface shows no kink around month-end and one-week implied volatility fell 0.64 points into 1 September.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: AUD/JPY and NZD/JPY would move most on a risk-off outcome; USD/JPY on the flow

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Tankan, September survey
key_catalysts.rationale: The most important Japanese economic indicator. The June survey had large manufacturers at +22, the best since 2018, and large non-manufacturers at +37, the best since August 1991, with FY2026 capex plans revised up 7.2 points to +11.5%. Critically it will update the corporate USD/JPY planning assumption, which was 152.57 in June against a spot testing 160.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. The BoJ release calendar has not been confirmed for the exact date, so this is dated to the first week of October per standard practice and flagged as such.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY; the planning-rate revision is a direct input to corporate hedging flow

key_catalysts.rationale: No projections at this meeting. If September delivered a hike, October is the first read on whether the Committee intends a sequence or a one-off, and the June SEP median of 3.8% for end-2026 implies only one further move from 3.625%.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially. The market prices two hikes by March 2027, so a pause here would be a modest dovish surprise.

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan decision and quarterly Outlook Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The last clearly yen-supportive scheduled event before the calendar turns hostile in November and December. The July Outlook already has FY2027 core CPI revised up to 2.4% and describes CPI risks as skewed to the upside; the October revision will incorporate a terms-of-trade shock, a weaker yen than the JPY 152.57 corporate planning rate and the subsidy unwind.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. Outlook Report forecast revisions are consistently under-anticipated and this one has an unusually clear upward skew.

key_catalysts.rationale: A binary political event in a year that has already seen two federal shutdowns and a Supreme Court ruling against IEEPA tariffs. Treasury Secretary Bessent has publicly linked yen volatility to US borrowing costs ahead of the midterms, which is why the US intervened jointly in July - so the election also marks the point after which the US political incentive to support the yen weakens.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced in the volatility surface: six-month implied of 7.85% is only 0.34 points above three-month despite containing this event.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY; risk crosses on any post-election volatility

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The projection round that will either confirm or retire the hike-now-cut-later shape - a 2026 median of 3.8% against a 2027 median of 3.6%. A 2027 median revised UP would remove the strategic differential-compression argument that carries this dossier's largest positive contribution.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. The market prices two hikes by March 2027 but has no view on the 2027 dots.

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision
key_catalysts.rationale: On current pricing the market has an implied 1.21% after this meeting, meaning a second 2026 hike is only lightly priced. Half of 36 surveyed economists now name 1.75% as terminal and 35 of 54 expect at least 1.50% by end-March 2027, so a December move would be a genuine repricing rather than a confirmation.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. This is the single largest identified gap between guidance and market pricing in the dossier.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Every yen cross; CHF/JPY and SEK/JPY most cleanly on the differential

key_catalysts.event: Japan FY2027 draft budget Cabinet approval
key_catalysts.rationale: Ministry requests total approximately JPY 143trn with a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line at a 3.8% assumed rate, and the Prime Minister has said he aims to cap new bond issuance at approximately JPY 40trn against JPY 29.6trn in the FY2026 initial budget. This is the specific event that decides whether the fiscal channel or the policy channel dominates the yen in 2027.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially. The 30-year JGB at 4.09-4.14% and the inverted 25s30s show the bond market is pricing fiscal risk; the FX market is not.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY; also GBP/JPY, where the counterpart has its own long-end fiscal premium

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan decision and quarterly Outlook Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The projection round that sets the FY2027 and first FY2029 forecasts and, on the consensus path, is the meeting at which the policy rate reaches 1.50%. It also falls immediately before the Japanese fiscal year-end repatriation window opens.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially. Economists expect at least 1.50% by end-March 2027 but the OIS curve has not fully discounted it.

key_catalysts.rationale: The first full quarter of data covering the post-hike period and the terms-of-trade shock. Private consumption contributed nothing to Q2 growth and business investment fell 1.2%, so a second consecutive weak domestic-demand quarter would begin to constrain the BoJ's path. Dated to the second week of February per standard Cabinet Office practice and flagged as such.

invalidators.condition: The Bank of Japan holds at 1.00% on 18 September 2026 without explicit language committing to a near-term move
invalidators.mechanism: Approximately 80-90% of a hike is priced, so a hold is a 25bp dovish surprise delivered directly into the heaviest factor in the dossier. It would also be read as the Board yielding to fiscal pressure from a JPY 36.6trn debt-service line, which converts Factor 8 from a background drag into the dominant driver and turns the entire policy-versus-fiscal tension in the bearish direction.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Bank of Japan Statement on Monetary Policy and the 2-year JGB yield
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Once, on 18 September; then daily on the 2-year
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Policy rate unchanged at 1.00% and the 2-year JGB falling below 1.60%

invalidators.condition: Brent crude sustains above USD 105 for four consecutive weeks on a full closure of the Strait of Hormuz
invalidators.mechanism: Japan imports essentially all of its hydrocarbons; mineral fuels were 22.1% of July imports and rose 53.5% year on year on falling volumes. A move from USD 93 to above USD 105 would push the terms-of-trade index below 78 from 81.62 and make consecutive monthly current-account deficits the base case, which removes the structural-surplus assumption underpinning every bullish yen argument.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Brent front month and the Japanese monthly trade balance
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Brent daily; trade balance monthly on the 15th-20th
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Brent above USD 105 for 20 consecutive trading days, or a Japanese monthly trade deficit wider than JPY 900bn

invalidators.condition: The 30-year JGB yield rises above 4.50% while USD/JPY simultaneously rises above 162.00
invalidators.mechanism: This specific combination is the definitive proof that Japanese yields are rising on fiscal risk premium rather than policy expectation. In a policy-driven repricing the yen strengthens as yields rise; if both rise together, the market is demanding compensation for Japanese sovereign risk and the differential argument that carries this dossier's largest positive contribution stops working entirely.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: 30-year JGB compound yield from the Ministry of Finance daily file, paired with USD/JPY spot
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: 30-year JGB above 4.50% (currently 4.092%) with USD/JPY above 162.00 on the same close

invalidators.condition: CFTC leveraged-fund net yen short exceeds -115,000 contracts while USD/JPY is below 158.00
invalidators.mechanism: That combination would mean fast money is rebuilding an extreme short into a market that is already moving against it, which is the classic pre-squeeze configuration. The current -77,042 at the 33rd percentile provides no signal; -115,000 matches the 30 June 2026 extreme, at which point the July squeeze covered 41,165 contracts in a single week.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures report, leveraged funds net position
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly, released Friday for the prior Tuesday
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Leveraged-fund net below -115,000 contracts with USD/JPY below 158.00

invalidators.condition: The Federal Reserve signals a pause or cut at the 16 September or 28 October meeting while the Bank of Japan continues hiking
invalidators.mechanism: The differential is the dominant factor at both horizons and it currently compresses only from the Japanese leg. A US pause would compress it from both ends simultaneously, taking the six-month forward differential from roughly 230bp toward 200bp or below. July payrolls at -23,000 with 103,000 of downward revisions is the data that would justify it.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: FOMC statement language and CME FedWatch implied probabilities
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Fed funds unchanged at 3.50-3.75% on 16 September with the December hike probability falling below 30%

invalidators.condition: Japan national core CPI falls below 1.5% year on year in either the September or October release
invalidators.mechanism: The entire bullish inflation case rests on the subsidy unwind lifting core clearly above 2% from the second half of fiscal 2026. A print below 1.5% would mean the queued rice disinflation - JA Niigata set the 2026-crop provisional payment 38% below last year - is arriving faster than the energy pass-through, which would let the BoJ pause after September and remove roughly half of the tactical positive contribution.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Statistics Bureau national CPI excluding fresh food; Tokyo CPI as a one-month lead
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly; Tokyo on the last Friday, national on the third Friday
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: National core below 1.5%, or Tokyo core below 1.6% as the lead indicator

invalidators.condition: A Big Three rating agency moves Japan's outlook to negative
invalidators.mechanism: Moody's A1, S&P A+ and Fitch A are all stable with no Big Three action in 2026, which is a striking gap against a JPY 143trn budget request, a widening IMF deficit path to -4.0% of GDP by 2031 and a 3.8% assumed interest rate. An outlook change would validate the fiscal risk premium already visible in the inverted 25s30s and force the FX market to price what the JGB market already has.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Moody's, S&P Global and Fitch sovereign rating actions on Japan
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Continuous; agencies typically act around budget approval
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Any Big Three outlook change to negative, or a downgrade

invalidators.condition: USD/JPY closes below the 200-week moving average at 148.792 for two consecutive weeks
invalidators.mechanism: The 200-week has not been breached from above in the current cycle, its slope is a positive 0.098 per week and there are zero weeks since the last close above it. A sustained break would mark the end of the multi-year yen bear market and would require the differential compression to have become self-reinforcing through the life-insurer hedge-ratio channel rather than depending on official flow.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: USD/JPY weekly close against the 200-week moving average from the gated price store
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Two consecutive Friday closes below 148.792 (level rising approximately 0.098 per week)

factors_changed.reason: Stance unchanged, confidence materially higher. On 1 August the BoJ had just held and September was priced near 23%; it is now 80-90% priced with Takata dissenting for 1.25%, the 2-year JGB has risen to a 31-year high of 1.743% and the economist terminal distribution has moved to 1.75%. The UST-JGB 10-year spread narrowed from 187bp to 180.7bp.

The largest single stance change in the dossier and a two-notch tactical downgrade for the yen. VIX fell from 17.09 at the 47.6th percentile of its one-year range to 14.51, close to the 2026 low of 14.13; US high-yield spreads tightened 21bp to 263bp; the S&P 500 is up 13.1% year to date and the Nikkei 58.4% over twelve months. This is now the most carry-friendly and therefore most yen-hostile risk configuration of the year.

A clean signpost resolution. Combined leveraged-fund and asset-manager net short has fallen from -176,091 contracts to -97,158 after the July intervention forced 41,165 contracts of covering in one week. The previous cycle's Bullish call rested on a stretched short; that short is now at the 33rd percentile with a z-score of -0.56 and generates no tactical signal. The strategic Bullish is retained on the life-insurer hedge-ratio channel, not on futures positioning.

Intervention moved from a possibility to a demonstrated, repeatable and now bilateral policy. Japan spent JPY 15,399.3bn between 30 July and 26 August including the first joint yen-buying operation with the US Treasury in decades - the cited source describes it as the first coordinated US-Japan FX action since 2011 - the Finance Minister said Japan 'will not hesitate to conduct further joint intervention', and the US Treasury Secretary repeated the commitment at the G20 on 31 August. With spot back on the defended 160 handle the tactical event distribution is asymmetric.

Downgraded because the structural picture deteriorated for the yen while the volatility picture improved. Spot has moved from 0.35% above the 200-day moving average to 1.07% above it, and the range percentile has risen to 79. Offsetting that, one-month implied volatility has risen from below 6.0% to 7.06% and we now have a sourced 25-delta risk reversal of -1.74 volatility points, which the previous cycle recorded as a gap.

The second two-notch downgrade and the direct consequence of the change in the Federal Reserve's stance. On 1 August the Fed was expected to ease; it is now priced at roughly 57-66% to HIKE on 16 September after Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole address, with the 2-year Treasury rising 11bp on the day - the largest Jackson Hole speech-day move in at least twenty years. SOFR sits exactly at interest on reserves, standing repo usage is nil and the Fed is buying bills to maintain ample reserves. Cheap, abundant dollars with a hawkish Fed is the yen's worst funding configuration.

factors_changed.factor: Factor 5 External Balance & Terms of Trade
factors_changed.reason: Stance unchanged, confidence materially higher on both horizons. Japan's mineral fuel import bill rose from JPY 2,101,701mn in June to JPY 2,680,352mn in July, the terms-of-trade index fell to 81.62 from 90.5 in the first quarter, June produced the first monthly current-account deficit in seventeen months and JKM LNG is up 101.9% year on year.

Stance unchanged, confidence higher. The FY2027 budget requests submitted on 31 August total approximately JPY 143trn with a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line at a 3.8% assumed rate, up from 3.0%, and the 10-year JGB touched 3.00% on 1 September for the first time since 1996. The 25s30s spread is now inverted.

Factor 2 is unchanged in both stance and confidence: national core moved from 1.6% to 1.8% and core-core from 1.7% to 1.9%, but the 2025 CPI rebasing cut measured inflation by roughly 0.2 percentage points, so the underlying acceleration is larger than the printed change and the two effects roughly offset in confidence terms. Factor 6 is upgraded on the 10 August Summary of Opinions, which contains materially more hawkish language than anything available at the previous cycle date.

signposts_triggered.outcome: Brent rose from USD 91.82 on 27 July to between USD 90.5 and USD 93.0 on 31 August depending on source; mineral fuel imports rose from JPY 2,101,701mn in June to JPY 2,680,352mn in July, and terms of trade fell to 81.62
signposts_triggered.implication: The invalidating threshold was approached but not crossed. The trade channel deteriorated on every measure, and this is the largest single contributor to the strategic bearish side of the score at -0.1024.

signposts_triggered.signpost: 30-year JGB yield as the fiscal risk-premium gauge
signposts_triggered.outcome: Rose from 3.971% to 4.092% on the Ministry of Finance basis and 4.135-4.14% on the vendor basis; 10s30s narrowed from 117.0bp to 114.9bp; 25s30s is now inverted at -1.0bp
signposts_triggered.implication: The confirming threshold - a 30-year FALLING below 3.90% while the 2-year rises - was not met; the opposite occurred. The inversion of 25s30s is new since the previous cycle and is the clearest single piece of evidence that the long end is pricing supply and fiscal risk rather than policy.

signposts_triggered.signpost: VIX and USD/JPY implied volatility as the carry-unwind gauge
signposts_triggered.outcome: VIX fell from 17.09 at the 47.6th percentile to 14.51 near the 2026 low; USD/JPY one-month implied rose from below 6.0% to 7.06%
signposts_triggered.implication: Both moved adversely for the yen in the sense that matters - lower realised risk aversion with higher option premia means the carry trade is comfortable while insurance has become more expensive. The previous cycle recorded the 25-delta risk reversal as a gap; it is now sourced at -1.74 volatility points, which is new information rather than a change.

conviction_change.explanation: A two-notch tactical downgrade and a one-notch strategic downgrade, with the weighted score falling from +0.3606 to +0.1270 tactically and from +0.1848 to +0.0940 strategically. Three changes account for almost all of it. First, Factor 4 went from Bullish 65 to Neutral 55 because the stretched short that justified the previous call was squeezed out in July - worth -0.065 tactically. Second, Factor 10 went from Bullish 52 to Bearish 58 because the Federal Reserve flipped from an expected easing path to a September hike priced at roughly 57-66% depending on source after Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole address - worth -0.121 tactically and -0.066 strategically. Third, Factor 3 went from Neutral 55 to Bearish 60 as VIX fell to 14.51 - worth -0.060 tactically. The bullish core of the thesis is intact and in places stronger: Policy, Inflation and Guidance all hold their Bullish stances with higher confidence than a month ago. What changed is everything around them.

new_catalysts: The 31 July 2026 joint Japan-US yen-buying intervention, the first coordinated US-Japan FX action since 2011, and the record JPY 15,399.3bn disclosed on 28 August for the 30 July-26 August window - taking 2026 to approximately JPY 27.1trn against a previous full-year record of JPY 15.32trn

Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole address on 28 August 2026, after which the 2-year Treasury rose 11bp - the largest Jackson Hole speech-day move in at least twenty years - and the market moved to price two Fed HIKES by March 2027
The 10-year JGB touching 3.00% on 1 September 2026, the first time since September 1996, with the 2-year at a 31-year high and the 25s30s spread inverting
The FY2027 budget requests submitted on 31 August 2026 at approximately JPY 143trn with a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line on a 3.8% assumed interest rate, a 29-year high

US Treasury Secretary Bessent's public statements at the G20 in Asheville on 31 August 2026 that he expects the Japanese government and the BoJ to act in ways that strengthen the yen, and his reported direct approach to Governor Ueda and Finance Minister Katayama

The 10 August 2026 BoJ Summary of Opinions containing the formulation that 'the pace of policy interest rate hikes will be faster than market expectations' and that it is 'necessary for the Bank to accelerate the pace of adjustment'
change_since_last_report.thesis_trajectory: The thesis is WEAKENING since 2026-08-01 despite the Japanese policy case getting stronger, because everything external to Japan moved against the yen. A month ago the bullish call rested on a hiking BoJ, a stretched speculative short and an easing Federal Reserve. Today the BoJ case is stronger - a September hike is 80-90% priced against 23%, the terminal has moved to 1.75% and the Summary of Opinions talks about accelerating - but the short has been squeezed out, the Fed is hiking rather than cutting, VIX has fallen to near its 2026 low and Japan's terms of trade have deteriorated a further 2.2 points. The most important observation is not in any single factor: it is that the yen failed to hold a record joint intervention, failed to rally through a 30-year high in JGB yields and failed to respond to a narrowing UST-JGB spread. Three yen-positive impulses produced a net 1.0% depreciation. That is the evidence base for cutting conviction from 4 to 2 rather than merely trimming confidence, and no stance in this dossier was revised as a result of this comparison - the factor work was completed first.

seasonality.pattern: Two documented Japanese seasonal patterns fall inside the horizons. The first is the interim fiscal half-year close on 30 September, at which Japanese corporates and institutions close their books for the first half and generate repatriation and dividend-related flows; it falls squarely inside the 2-4 week tactical window. The second and much larger is the Japanese fiscal year-end on 31 March, which produces the best-documented seasonal repatriation pattern in G10 FX, with flows building through late February and March; the leading edge of that window falls at the very end of the 1-6 month strategic horizon.
seasonality.relevance_window: 30 September 2026 for the interim close - within the tactical horizon. Late February to 31 March 2027 for the full-year close - at the outer boundary of the strategic horizon, which runs to approximately 1 March 2027, so only the leading edge is captured.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: We deliberately do not quantify this. No dated source for the historical magnitude of Japanese fiscal year-end repatriation flows was obtained in this research cycle, and the currency brief describes the pattern qualitatively as 'well-documented' without a figure. Asserting a pip magnitude would be fabrication. What can be stated with a source is the current scale of the underlying flow: Japanese residents sold a net JPY 1,978.4bn of foreign bonds in a single week in August, so the weekly flow capacity is measured in trillions of yen.
seasonality.current_alignment: Aligned with the thesis on both horizons, but weakly. The 30 September interim close adds a modest repatriation bid at exactly the point where our tactical path expectation has the yen consolidating after the September central bank cluster, which is supportive. The March 2027 pattern sits beyond our base-case window and is one reason the strategic path expectation has the third phase, January to March, as yen-supportive. The important caveat is that life-insurer hedge ratios are at historic lows, which means a higher share of any repatriation flow hits spot rather than rolling off existing forwards - so the seasonal effect should be larger than usual this year, not smaller.

assumptions: Spot and derived analytics are taken from the gated price store, whose tail is 2026-08-28 on a weekday-only basis. USD/JPY is therefore quoted at 160.115 throughout for internal consistency across the cycle, with the 2026-09-01 print of 160.126 noted where relevant. All moving averages, realised volatilities, ATR, range percentiles and support and resistance zones are read from the store's derived file rather than recomputed, so that they match the figures the downstream pair analysis will use.

The BIS real effective exchange rate of 65.3 is for period June 2026 and is 63 days old at the valuation date, marginally outside the 60-day strategic freshness window. Its historical percentile of 2 is an ESTIMATE - the cache carries the level and the one-year change but not the distribution - and is flagged in the valuation section as best available rather than sourced.

The PPP deviation table is NOT a purchasing-power-parity calculation. No PPP source exists in the free stack. What is presented is a relative BIS REER gap against the 2020 base period, mechanically translated into an implied cross rate, and it is labelled as such in every row. It should be read as a relative real-exchange-rate comparison, not a fair-value estimate.

Sovereign 10-year yields for the nine non-Japanese peers are taken from the cached IRLTLT01 monthly series with an as-of date of 2026-06-01, which is 92 days old and breaches both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows. They are used only for cross-currency comparability and are labelled with their as-of date at every occurrence. The Japanese 10-year is quoted from the Ministry of Finance daily file at 2.943% for 2026-08-31 and must not be paired with a peer leg from the monthly series in any single spread calculation.

There is a documented 4-5 basis point discrepancy on the 30-year JGB and roughly 11 basis points on the 40-year between the Ministry of Finance compound-yield series and vendor on-the-run quotes. Ministry of Finance figures are used throughout for curve mathematics; vendor levels are quoted alongside where the difference is material.

The three-month USD/JPY cross-currency basis of approximately -20 basis points is a DERIVATION, not a quote. It is obtained as the difference between the cached futures-implied roll premium of -282.2 basis points annualised and the 262.5 basis point policy differential. No quoted cross-currency basis level for USD/JPY or EUR/USD could be sourced from any free provider, and this is recorded as the dossier's largest unresolved data gap.

Forward outrights are constructed from the same -282.2 basis point annualised roll premium on an actual/365 basis. They are model forwards derived from a cached futures observation of 2026-08-26, not dealer quotes, and the 1-month, 3-month and 6-month outrights of 159.744, 158.989 and 157.862 should be treated as approximations accurate to a few pips.

The one-year implied volatility percentile of approximately 40 is an ESTIMATE. No dated implied-volatility history for USD/JPY was sourceable; the estimate is anchored on the observation that the current one-month level of 7.06% sits between the sub-6.0% readings of late July and the levels seen during the intervention episode. Flagged as best available.

Japan CPI is a known structural gap in the cache because the OECD prices flow returns 404 for Japan and FRED redistribution ceased in 2021. The figures used - 1.9% headline, 1.8% core, 1.9% core-core for July 2026 - are taken from the cached calendar events file, which carries the released prints, and corroborated through research. The core-core figure carries an unresolved source conflict between 1.8% and 1.9% and 1.9% is used, with the alternative flagged.

The Statistics Bureau rebased the CPI to 2025 weights with the July 2026 release, which lowered measured inflation by approximately 0.2 percentage points. Any year-on-year comparison spanning July 2026 is vintage-inconsistent and this is noted wherever a trajectory is discussed.

Macro comparison table figures for the ten non-Japanese currencies are point-in-time OECD and Eurostat vintages as visible on the valuation date, drawn from the cache so that all eleven rows share a source basis. Several are stale: EUR, CHF, NOK and SEK CPI are 2025-Q4 observations and AUD and NZD GDP are 2026-Q1. Core CPI is absent from the vintage store for every currency except the United States and Japan and is recorded as null with the intended measure named, rather than proxied with a headline figure.

Singapore has no cached vintages because it is not an OECD member, and no policy rate exists because MAS operates an S$NEER band. All SGD macro cells are null by design. This is a structural gap, not a research failure.

The cached CFTC tranche of 2026-08-11 was 21 days old at the valuation date. The positioning figures used throughout are the current 2026-08-25 report obtained by research directly from the CFTC, which supersedes it. The cached dealer net of +23,257 for 2026-08-11 could not be reconciled with a derived +43,970 for 2026-08-18 and is flagged as unverified; it is not used anywhere in this dossier.

The current account of 5.04% of GDP for 2026-Q2 is taken from the cached vintage store but could not be verified against any quarterly current-account-to-GDP source in research. The OECD annual figure of 4.70% for 2025 is the corroborating anchor. Flagged as best available.

The operative US tariff rate on Japanese motor vehicles could not be established from a primary source. Two candidates circulate - 15% under the 2025 framework agreement and 12.5% under a post-litigation Section 301 construction - and neither could be confirmed from the Federal Register, USTR or a tier-one wire. No rate is asserted anywhere in this dossier and the uncertainty is stated in Factor 7.

G10 and SGD policy rates and all scheduled central bank decision dates are taken exclusively from the cached central-bank meetings file, which is authoritative. No scheduled decision date in this dossier was obtained by web search.

Two catalysts use week-level dating because exact dates could not be confirmed: the September BoJ Tankan is dated 2026-10-W1 on the basis of the Bank's stated practice of releasing at the beginning of October, and Japan's Q4 2026 GDP first preliminary is dated 2027-02-W2 on standard Cabinet Office practice. The FY2027 draft budget approval is dated 2026-12-W4 on the FY2026 precedent of 26 December 2025.

Bank consensus forecasts are drawn from an aggregator covering 23 desks plus individually sourced primary pages for MUFG, Scotiabank, Goldman Sachs and RBC. Named targets attributed only through the aggregator - notably Nomura's 165.50 - are flagged as aggregator-sourced. A widely circulated claim of a J.P. Morgan target of 164 rests on secondary sources dated December 2025 and is not used.

Japan's 5-year sovereign credit default swap spread could not be sourced from any free provider and is recorded as a gap in Factor 8. Sovereign ratings are taken from a live aggregator rather than from agency primary pages, which are JavaScript-rendered and could not be fetched, and the Fitch action date of 19 January 2026 is described as a periodic affirmation whose commentary text was not retrieved.

No Bank of Japan Governor speech or Diet testimony in English is available for August 2026. The most recent Ueda texts are dated 3 June and 27 May 2026 and were not retrieved. The guidance analysis therefore rests on the 31 July press conference as reported by Reuters, the 10 August Summary of Opinions, and Deputy Governor Himino's 27 August speech.

The G10+SGD rankings are computed against this cycle's completed weighted scores for AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR and GBP. Placement of USD, NOK, NZD, SEK and SGD is a reasoned estimate because those dossiers have not yet been built for the 2026-09-01 cycle, and this is stated in the ranking commentary for both horizons.

Phase 6 adversarial verification was run on 2026-09-01 against the cited URLs. It confirmed the BoJ policy decision and vote, the full JGB curve for 2026-08-31, the UST-JGB spread arithmetic, every CFTC positioning figure, the MoF intervention total, all ten implied-volatility and risk-reversal quotes, the bank and Reuters consensus figures, the 2026 shunto tally and the July trade and terms-of-trade data, and it independently reproduced every weighted-score contribution, all nine carry spreads and all three forward outrights. It flagged the following, each of which is now marked inline and has produced a confidence reduction in the affected factor: the 160.115 spot anchor is a gated-store weekday close that vendor sources do not corroborate (Factor 9 tactical confidence cut 55 to 53, strategic 52 to 50); September FOMC pricing is uncited and the corroborated same-day reading is nearer 57% than 66% (Factor 1 tactical confidence cut 58 to 56); the sole citation supporting the VIX, equity, credit-spread and commodity block is a client-rendered live blog that returns an empty body (Factor 3 tactical cut 62 to 60 and strategic 52 to 50, Factor 5 tactical cut 60 to 58 and strategic 66 to 64); and the IMF debt and deficit figures and the sovereign ratings are uncited (Factor 8 strategic cut 64 to 62). It also corrected an error in the executive summary that described the 163.980 fifty-two-week HIGH as a low, four carry-table ordinal errors, a mis-attributed '29-year' superlative, a claim that the 31 July operation was the first coordinated action since 1998 when the cited source says 2011, and the presentation of June wage data inside a July-labelled line. Anything the verifier could not confirm is marked 'best available, flagged' in the text rather than presented as solid.
